title: Injunction applications - how to actually get an ex-parte order
p1:
Most people think getting an urgent court injunction is simply about proving you are right.

That is not how ex-parte orders are usually won.
p2:
The surprising part? The court is not deciding the whole case at that stage. It is deciding whether there is enough urgency and risk that waiting could cause serious harm.

Many applications fail because they focus on the dispute, not the need for immediate protection.
p3:
A strong ex-parte application shows three things clearly: there is a real issue to be decided, delay could cause damage, and the applicant has been honest about all important facts, including the ones that may not help their case.

The practical takeaway: urgency must be demonstrated, not simply claimed. A judge needs a clear reason why action is needed now, before the other side is heard.
conclusion: What do you think is the biggest mistake people make when applying for an ex-parte injunction: proving the case or proving the urgency?
